description.narrative:
Quote from the 'Revised Project Document Amendment and Extension to August 2024, Regional Stabilisation Facility for Lake Chad, August 2021':
'While robust national and multi-national military operations have re-taken territory previously controlled by Boko Haram and factions, a new approach is required to consolidate these gains and establish the conditions necessary to transition from military to civilian responsibility for security. The RSF is a rapidresponse mechanism that relevant authorities can sequence with military operations. The first phase of the Regional Stabilisation Facility concentrated on two results areas:
- Immediate stabilization of specific areas, cleared of Boko Haram and other armed group control, but where communities remain vulnerable to continued infiltration and attack; and
- Initiation of extended stabilization activities across the Boko Haram-affected States and Regions, through support, to implement the Lake Chad Basin Commission (LCBC) Regional Stabilisation Strategy.
The amended and extended Regional Stabilisation Facility builds on the results and lessons learned of the nearly first two years of RSF implementation, resulting in a clear proof of concept. The extended phase will thus focus on increasing the scale of stabilisation by connecting, enlarging, or increasing the number of intervention sites. Stabilisation achievements will be consolidated, and the ground prepared for a handover to peace-building and development actors. The Facilitys overall objective is to improve the social contract in insurgency-affected areas of the Lake Chad Basin. As in the previous phase, the Facility is divided into immediate and extended stabilisation. Under the immediate stabilisation outcome "Community stability and State presence increased in JAP locations", which is at the centre of the first 18 months in each site, 3 outputs contribute to the expected results:
1.1 Community security and justice systems established and operational in JAP (Joint Action Plan) locations,
1.2 Essential social services infrastructure constructed and/or rehabilitated, functional, and accessible,
1.3. Targeted households provided with livelihood opportunities.
The extended stabilisation outcome the post-immediate stabilisation phase has 4 outputs with the aim to support local, national, and regional stabilisation structures to oversee, coordinate, and implement stabilisation and recovery efforts:
2.1 Stabilisation actors have knowledge to consolidate the stabilization achievements and promote social cohesion,
2.2. Improved cross-border coordination and cooperation,
2.3 LCBC capacity developed to steer and support RSS (i.e. the LCBC Regional Strategy for the Stabilisation, Recovery and Resilience of the Boko Haram affected Areas of the Lake Chad Basin) implementation and governance structures,
2.4 Improved LCBC coordination and oversight of TAP [Territorial Action Plan] implementation, The amended and extended phase of the RSF has furthermore a stronger focus on conflict sensitivity and gender.'

Detta är ett finansiellt stöd till förlängingsfasen (2022-2024) av UNDPs regionala stabiliseringsfacilitet för Tchadsjö-regionen. Sida stöttade även den första fase med icke-öronmärkta medel och bedömer att det finns starka skäl att förlänga insatsen för att stärka uppnådda result och lämna över till lokala myndigheter.

This is a financial support to the extension phase (2022-2024) of UNDP's Regional Stabilization Facility for the Lake Chad region. Sida supported the first phase with non-earmarked funds and assesses that there are strong reasons to prolong the support in order to reinforce the achieved results and hand-over to local authorities.

description.narrative:
The following results can be found in the RSF final cumulative report of the previous phase, 2021-2024:
- Between 2021 and 2024, the RSF supported stabilization efforts in 33 sites across the four countries of the Lake Chad Basin: Cameroon, Chad, Niger, and Nigeria. Cumulatively, an estimated 1,370,000 people have benefitted from RSF interventions, including approximately 730,000 women.
- In Nigeria, the deployment of security personnel increased by 89% following the construction and rehabilitation of offices and residences for law enforcement agencies, reducing dependency on the military for civilian policing and dispute resolution.
- In Cameroon alone, more than 28,000 youths and children are now enrolled in schools constructed via the RSF, while overall more than one million inhabitants across the four countries of the Lake Chad Basin are able to access health services thanks to the construction and quipping of medical centers in RSF sites.
- In Guitté (Chad), a notable innovation was the establishment of a Woman's Platform building a multifunctional space designed to foster women's inclusion in economic and community life. It provides a safe environment for women to meet, store goods, and process and market agricultural and fishery products.
- During the 202124 programming phase, over 1,700 government officials and members of local structures were trained on topics related to social cohesion, gender equity, and participatory planning.
- The RSF provided technical and logistical support to the organization of four Steering Committee meetings of the Regional Strategy for Stabilization, Recovery and Resilience (RS SRR). These gatherings enabled members and partners to jointly analyze the regional security situation, assess implications for stabilization programming, and take strategic decisions on the implementation of the Strategy. One of the most significant outcomes of this period was the adjustment and extension of the RS SRR for a new six-year period (20252030).
Throughout the last phase, UNDP adopted strategies to move beyond 'islands of stability' in the Join Action Plan (JAP) locations towards broader networks/corridors but has so far failed to do so. These networks/corridors have an increased focus in the current phase using the Territorial Action Plans (TAPs, currently under revision) as an entry point. Sida should continue to follow UNDP's efforts to implement strategies and methods to achieve this.
Given that this is the last phase support, solid analysis should be available on what makes exiting the JAP locations possible and what criteria need to be in place for a successful handover to government counterparts. This has so far not been the case and UNDP needs to give the issue of 'exits' from JAPs more attention.
